commands.name: init
commands.usage: init [--adopt] [--name n] [--base b] [--bundle dir] [--run level=command]… [--overwrite path]… [--system-code c] [--org o] [--zone z]
commands.does: ask questions, write the profile, render templates, vendor the CLI

commands.name: upgrade
commands.does: re-vendor the CLI from the installed plugin's release

commands.name: index
commands.does: regenerate every index.md in the bundle

commands.name: check
commands.does: OKF validation, plan lint, profile lint

commands.name: status
commands.does: print the state table

commands.name: next
commands.does: print the single next action

commands.name: lane
commands.does: print the computed lane and why

commands.name: card
commands.does: render the bolt card

commands.name: start
commands.does: name the worktree branch unit/U-<n> and check its base

commands.name: approve
commands.does: stamp approval (owner only)

commands.name: delegate
commands.does: let the lead approve re-approvals or quick-lane bolts (owner only)

commands.name: mode
commands.does: record the owner's run mode: unattended or not, the next action to stop at, where to report (owner only)

commands.name: research
commands.does: print the researcher's brief for a question held on the doc

commands.name: review
commands.does: print an intent reviewer's brief, or store a reviewer verdict keyed by diff hash or by the reviewed docs' hash

commands.name: report
commands.does: store the builder's report (JSON from the file, or stdin)

commands.name: hold
commands.does: record or release an owner hold in the plan

commands.name: priority
commands.does: record an owner priority in the plan

commands.name: persona
commands.does: print a role persona and its knowledge, for the lead to work in

commands.name: name
commands.usage: name <kind> [--domain d] [--role r] [--env e] [--verb v] [--stage s] [--action a] [--table t] [--object o] [--number n] [--metric m] [--bolt u] [--section s] [--key k] [--date d] [--preview] [--tag t]
commands.does: print a name from the naming grammar and registry

commands.name: fact
commands.does: run a read-only probe on the target and record its output as a platform fact

commands.name: dispose
commands.does: record the owner's disposition of a review finding

commands.name: new
commands.does: write a draft bolt B-<n> under bolts/, the next free number, named from its title

commands.name: fix
commands.does: create a one-bolt plan without an intent

commands.name: map
commands.does: write the codebase map in the bundle (merge also writes it)

commands.name: push
commands.does: push the base after checking its new commits

commands.name: merge
commands.does: run the merge gate, then merge --no-ff with trailers

commands.name: hook
commands.does: entry point for hooks; reads the hook JSON on stdin

messages.cardDeps: Your scope pins dependencies ({{manifests}}). Your training data is out of date: look up each version you add or bump from its registry or official release page, take the newest stable release that fixes every known advisory, pin it exactly, and list it in your report as "deps": [{"name", "version", "source"}] (the URL or command that showed it). The merge gate, CI and the daily run check currency and advisories live: {{checks}}; a test of yours never queries a registry, it proves a check on fixed inputs offline.
messages.cardPlatform:
The deploy target is already defined in: {{refs}}
Build on its conventions (names, namespaces, registries, access); add nothing it already provides, and stop and report if the bolt needs a change there.
messages.cardDataRest:
- shared, for any module: {{shared}}
Reach any other data only through its owning module's interface, an event or a shared service; the merge gate fails a direct read or write (ARCH-DATA).
messages.cardDesign: the # {{sections}} section(s) of {{path}} at the base
messages.planIncrementWaiver: {{unit}} reaches the product ({{glob}} overlaps {{area}}), but {{intent}} skips its end-to-end test with endToEnd:
messages.planIncrementUnit: {{unit}} crosses modules {{modules}} but tests only at the {{level}} level
messages.planGenerated: {{unit}} scope names {{has}} but not {{lacks}}: a generator links them
messages.planUntracked: {{unit}} scope names {{path}}, which exists but git does not track: a builder cannot commit it
messages.planDecision: {{unit}} touches the one-way door {{door}} through scope {{glob}} and links no decision{{bare}}
messages.planDecisionBare: (a bare name matches at any depth: write /{{glob}} for the root file)
messages.scopeApproval: {{path}}: approvals and verified_hash are the owner's
messages.secretFound: {{path}} contains what looks like a secret
messages.modelCard: {{agent}} for {{unit}} has no brief to read: {{why}}
messages.guardSubagent: {{agent}} may not run aidlc {{command}}; its role runs {{allowed}}
messages.docsRestamped: generated.at {{from}} was not the current UTC time; the docs hook set it to {{to}}: re-read the file before editing it again
messages.statusResume: Load the aidlc skill and run aidlc next.
messages.nextMigrate: elaborate the migration intent with the owner in {{dir}}/I-1-<slug>.md (adopted at {{commit}}): docs, always-on context, profile, architecture baseline, data owners, naming rules, module audit, cleanup; then ask for approval
messages.nextStopped: the builder of {{unit}} stopped ({{reason}}): if the bolt doc is wrong, fix it and ask the owner to re-approve it; otherwise remove the cause and start its builder again (card: aidlc card {{unit}})
messages.runLine: {{mode}}{{#each stop}}, stop at {{this}}{{/each}}{{#each report}}, report to {{this}}{{/each}}
messages.notDelegatedAcs: {{name}} changes its acceptance criteria: the owner approves it
messages.priorityUsage: usage: priority <bolt> <n>, a whole number; higher builds first
messages.nextAutoApprove: approve {{docs}}, delegated by the owner: aidlc approve --auto {{docs}}
messages.notDelegated: {{name}} is not in a class the owner delegated (approvals.auto in .aidlc/local/profile.json): the owner approves it
messages.nextGated: the gate refused {{unit}} ({{codes}}; aidlc merge {{unit}} lists them): fix what the lead can, ask the owner for the rest
messages.promptApproved:
The owner typed this approval; the prompt hook ran it:
{{out}}Commit the stamps and continue with aidlc next; do not run aidlc approve for it.
messages.promptApproveFailed: The owner typed an approval, but it failed: {{error}}. Tell the owner; do not run aidlc approve for it.
messages.delegateUsage: usage: delegate <class>… | off [--until <date>], classes: reapprove, quick, upgrade

OKF-FM.fix: give the file a terminated --- block of YAML key: value pairs

OKF-TYPE.fix: add a non-empty type: to the frontmatter

HOUSE-DESC.fix: add title: and a one-sentence description:

HOUSE-LINK.fix: point the link at an existing file or remove it

DOC-SCHEMA.fix: add the keys the type requires (okf.bundle.schemas), use a value its list allows, and keep the doc in its type's folder (docs: Bundle v2)

DOC-SLUG.fix: rename the file to its id and the slug of its title (lower case, hyphens, no apostrophes, at most 48 characters, cut at a word), keeping the id; aidlc new names new docs this way

DOC-GENERATED.fix: never edit a generated doc: change what it is drawn from and let the CLI write it again (aidlc map, aidlc index, or the next merge); a request is never rewritten: restore it, and keep a changed request with a new aidlc intake

HOUSE-SIZE.fix: split the doc or move detail into linked docs

PROFILE-ARCH.fix: give each module its data globs and set architecture.graph (printing data edges) and architecture.data; add architecture.acyclic and each module's api (docs: Architecture model)

PROFILE-NAMES.fix: write the naming decision from .aidlc/templates/docs/naming.md; give each pattern a names rule: id, files globs, pattern, and a find regex whose first group is the name (none for a rule on paths)

PROFILE-RULE.fix: set docs.rules entries to a HOUSE-* code and one of error, warning, off

CONTRACT-NAME.fix: follow the API grammar of decision 0014: full lowerCamel names, Noun_Verb operation ids, a dated api-version, camelCase segments and properties, PascalCase enums, systemData on resources, nextLink on lists (aidlc name path|operation-id|api-version) (docs: Naming)

PROFILE-NAMING.fix: set naming.tokens (system: 2-6 lower-case letters or digits; org and zone: DNS labels), domains as lower-case plural nouns, vocabulary words as lower-case words, none of them banned (docs: Naming)

PROFILE-KIND.fix: give each module its kind (domain, pipeline, foundation, adapter, runtime, extension or delivery), surfaces from client, server and events, and system as core and extensions globs (docs: Architecture model)

PROFILE-KEY.fix: remove it, or use the key the profile doc names for what you meant

PLAN-DAG.fix: remove the cycle or point depends at an existing bolt

PLAN-AC.fix: give each AC in the bolt its own AC-<k>

PLAN-LEVEL.fix: write - AC-<k> (<level>): with a level from profile.levels

PLAN-RESERVE.fix: use <kind> <area>/<n> with a kind from profile.reserve and a number no other bolt holds

PLAN-SCOPE.fix: give the bolt a scope, narrow the scopes, or add a depends between the bolts

PLAN-SHARED.fix: drop it from the scope: merge regenerates indexes and the log and runs profile.regen for shared files

PLAN-REQ.fix: cite the requirements the intent or bolt serves: requirements: [R-<n>]

PLAN-TEST.fix: add a scope glob where the level's tests live, give the AC a level whose paths the scope holds, or add /.aidlc/profile.json to the scope so the bolt adds its test location to levels

PLAN-MODULE.fix: name a module from profile.modules, or add the module to the profile

PLAN-DEPENDS.fix: add the other bolt to depends, or move the AC to that bolt

PLAN-RUN.fix: add levels.<level>.run to .aidlc/profile.json, at least for unit and e2e

PLAN-PLATFORM.fix: find how the target is run today (an infra repo, its GitOps set-up, namespaces, registries, access) and list it in deploy.platform in .aidlc/profile.json, as paths or URLs; [] when this project defines its own target

PLAN-CARD.fix: shorten the bolt doc (ACs, Interfaces, Out of scope) or the project rules before the approval: card renders only an approved doc

PLAN-SKELETON.fix: cut a walking skeleton first: an early bolt that builds the top-level test harness and the thinnest real path through every stage, with a top-level AC; then each increment adds a top-level AC for what it adds

PLAN-RUNBOOK.fix: link a Runbook doc from the intent (template .aidlc/templates/docs/runbook.md: how to roll back, what to watch, who to call)

PLAN-BOLT.fix: move the work item to bolts/ as B-<n> (aidlc new bolt "<title>"); units/ holds only the bolts a v1 plan approved (docs: Increments and bolts)

PATHWAY-SKIP.fix: declare the intent's pathway (greenfield, feature, brownfield) and complete each step it requires before approval (docs: Inception)

INTENT-SIZE.fix: split the intent: at most 5 increments and 5 domains, each increment with its own success measure

ELAB-OPEN.fix: ask the owner and record the answer under the question: - Answer: <letter> …

ELAB-VAGUE.fix: ask the owner a follow-up with 2-3 options or a measure, and record their pick (docs: Elaboration checks)

ELAB-BARE.fix: record which option the owner chose, by its letter, then any words of theirs

DOMAIN-DATA.fix: give the table one owning domain; the others read it through that domain's client or events

DOMAIN-TERM.fix: give the term one meaning, or qualify it per domain (an order in sales, a purchase order in buying)

DOMAIN-REQ.fix: name the domains the requirement belongs to in its domains: key

FACT-MISSING.fix: probe the target with aidlc fact "<title>" -- <read-only command> and cite the fact in the decision's facts:

FACT-STALE.fix: probe again with aidlc fact and cite the new fact

DOC-AMEND.fix: restore the approved decision and write a new one with supersedes: <its number>; approving it marks the old one superseded

DECISION-HORIZON.fix: decide it when its increment is next but one; keep the intent's decisions to the increments being built

DESIGN-COHERENCE.fix: make the decisions agree: one domain per transaction and per table, dependencies the kind table allows, or a superseding decision

DOC-REF.fix: point the key at an existing doc of the right type, or remove it

PLAN-INCREMENT.fix: list the intent's increments under # Increments, each line opening with I-<n>.<k> and naming its bolts with a top-level AC among them, the walking skeleton first; no bolt waits on a later increment or a fix bolt (move what an increment needs into it); an intent without the section is one increment and runs end to end once with a top-level AC (or endToEnd: "<why>" outside every module and one-way door); a bolt crossing modules is tested at integration or higher (docs: Increments and bolts)

PLAN-DESIGN.fix: write the section before approval: Domain names the entities, the one domain owning each and how domains interact; Logical the services, interfaces and data shapes this bolt changes. Or set design: "<why none>" when the bolt adds no domain or logic

PLAN-GENERATED.fix: add the missing globs to the scope (the profile's generated entry pairs outputs with sources), or scope the tracked file instead of the untracked one

PLAN-DECISION.fix: link a Decision doc from the bolt (template .aidlc/templates/docs/decision.md: options, choice, why), for the owner to approve with it, or set twoWay: "<why it is easy to undo>" in its frontmatter

BOLT-BIND.fix: bind the bolt to one domain in modules, or to one horizontal module with neededBy: B-<v> naming a bolt of the same increment that binds a domain (docs: Construction by proof)

BOLT-SPAN.fix: split the bolt into one bolt per domain, or move it to increment 1, the walking skeleton (docs: Construction by proof)

INCR-SKELETON.fix: put on increment 1 a bolt with a top-level AC and a bolt binding the delivery module, so the skeleton runs end to end on its target (docs: Construction by proof)

FIX-SHAPE.fix: give the fix bolt exactly one AC, a regression test that fails before the fix, and a scope outside the decisions and one-way doors; a design change goes through a decision and an increment (docs: Construction by proof)

HATCH-EXPIRED.fix: close the escape hatch (merge or drop the fix bolt, end the waiver, supersede the exception), or the owner sets a later until (docs: Construction by proof)

intentTransitions: a merged increment ships: check, release, smoke
deploy check passes or none set
release on a pushed green base passes, smoke too or none set

GATE-APPROVAL.fix: the owner approves the bolt: they type approve <bolt>

SCOPE-OUT.fix: move the change into scope, or the lead widens the scope and the owner re-approves

GATE-LANE.fix: the lead raises the bolt's lane, re-renders the card and restarts the review

GATE-AC.fix: add a test tagged with the AC

GATE-LEVEL.fix: move the test under the level's paths in profile.levels, or add the paths the level lacks, in this bolt or in one merged before it

GATE-CHECK.fix: fix the module until its check passes

GATE-PROOF.fix: make each tagged test fail without the change, then report again

GATE-SKIP.fix: run the level where its tests can run (set what it needs), or make the skipped test run; a skipped test proves nothing

GATE-RUN.fix: the builder fixes the code or tests until the level's run passes on the base merged in

GATE-BASE.fix: not this bolt's to fix: draft a fix bolt for the base (aidlc fix); this merge waits for it

GATE-REVIEW.fix: run the reviewer on the current diff and card: aidlc review record

GATE-CARD.fix: render the card (aidlc card) and review against it

GATE-SPECIALIST.fix: run the reviewer with that focus on the current diff

GATE-OKF.fix: fix the doc, then run aidlc check

GATE-SECURITY.fix: fix what the security check reports

GATE-DEPENDENCY.fix: bump each flagged dependency to the newest stable release that fixes it, looked up from its registry, and report the source

ARCH-BOUNDARY.fix: remove the dependency, or the owner approves an exception decision; a bolt that adds a boundary lists the edges the base already has in its except decision, or its own merge fails

ARCH-CHECK.fix: fix what the architecture check reports

ARCH-KIND.fix: depend only on what the kind table allows (docs: Architecture model): a domain on foundation kits and other domains' client or events, never the core on an extension or product code on delivery; move the code, or the owner approves the edge as an exception

ARCH-LAYER.fix: point layers inward: interface to application and model, application to model, infrastructure to model; model depends only on foundation kits

ARCH-REACH.fix: split the domain's client from its internals so a runtime that only calls it links only the client (its surfaces), or host the domain in the runtime

ARCH-API.fix: call the module through its public paths, move what is needed into them, or the owner approves the edge in the architecture.api.except decision with a fix bolt

ARCH-CYCLE.fix: break the circle: move the shared part into its own module, or let one side publish an event the other reads; or the owner approves a module edge in the architecture.acyclic.except decision with a fix bolt

ARCH-DATA.fix: go through the owning module (interface, event or shared service), give the data one owner, or the owner approves the edge in the architecture.data.except decision with a fix bolt

GATE-SHARED.fix: revert the change; merge writes indexes, logs and shared files

GATE-CONFLICT.fix: merge the base into the bolt branch, resolve, and report again

CI-DEPENDENCY.fix: plan a fix bolt (aidlc fix) that bumps each flagged dependency to the newest stable release, looked up from its registry

CI-MERGE.fix: merge bolts only with aidlc merge

CI-COMMIT.fix: commit code only through bolts; direct commits may touch only docs and workflow files

PUSH-COMMIT.fix: move the change into a bolt; direct commits may touch only docs and workflow files

GATE-SECRET.fix: remove the secret from the bolt branch; read it from the environment

GATE-IDENTITY.fix: use the runtime's workload identity: mTLS or a token bound to it, a database role reached with short-lived certificates or tokens, federated credentials outside the cluster; a throwaway password belongs in a test path

GATE-NAME.fix: rename it to match the rule's pattern; if the rule is wrong, the owner changes its decision and the profile first

CONTRACT-NAME.fix: follow the API grammar of decision 0014 (aidlc name path|operation-id|api-version), or change the naming decision first

TERM-SYNONYM.fix: use the glossary's term; if the domain's language changed, change its domain doc's glossary first (docs: Naming)

PROOF-AC.fix: make the reverted tree compile (keep the interfaces, revert the behaviour), or report a mutation per AC (docs: Construction by proof)

REVIEW-SECURITY.fix: the owner disposes of each finding: aidlc dispose <B-n> F-<k> fixed|accepted "<reason>" [--until <date>] (docs: Construction by proof)

INCR-DONE.fix: release increment 1 and pass its smoke on the target first (docs: Construction by proof)

GUARD-FORCE.fix: push without force; history on shared branches is never rewritten

GUARD-PUSH.fix: push the base with aidlc push

GUARD-BASE-DELETE.fix: the base branch is never deleted

GUARD-NOVERIFY.fix: commit with hooks; fix what they report

GUARD-BASE-COMMIT.fix: commit code only in a bolt worktree; on the base commit only docs

GUARD-MERGING.fix: wait for the merge to end, then commit; a merge that died leaves .git/aidlc/merging, which counts for two hours, or remove it

GUARD-BASE-MOVE.fix: the base moves only by aidlc merge and aidlc push

GUARD-ALIAS.fix: run the git command by its own name

GUARD-HOOK.fix: Claude Code runs the hooks; the agent never runs aidlc hook

SCOPE-STATE.fix: leave the state to the aidlc command that records it

GUARD-OWNER.fix: allow the prompt to run it, deny to refuse; in a terminal the owner can also type it with !

GUARD-RELEASE.fix: the owner confirms tags and releases

SCOPE-OUT.fix: stop and report; the lead widens the scope

SCOPE-SHARED.fix: leave indexes, logs and shared files to aidlc merge

GUARD-SCHEDULE.fix: only the owner approves: they type approve <doc>

SCOPE-APPROVAL.fix: only the owner approves: they type approve <doc>

SECRET.fix: keep secrets out of the repo; read them from the environment

MODEL-UNIT.fix: name the bolt U-<n> in the prompt and start it from its card

MODEL-MISMATCH.fix: pass the model the card names (aidlc card)

GUARD-SUBAGENT.fix: leave it to the lead: a subagent runs only its role's aidlc commands (hooks.subagentCommands) and returns its result

pages.title: Codebase map
pages.description: The codebase as a tree of module folders, with the data each module owns and its public paths; written at every merge, never by hand.

pages.title: Module dependencies
pages.description: A C4 component view of which module depends on which, from the dependency graph; written at every merge, never by hand.

pages.title: Module dependency table
pages.description: Each module with the modules it uses and the modules that use it; written at every merge, never by hand.

pages.title: Domains and layers
pages.description: A C4 component view by kind, with the domains side by side with their layers, and the horizontal kinds as bands across them, as a diagram and a matrix of paths; written at every merge, never by hand.

steps.questions: every question answered by an option
steps.domains: a domain doc for each of its domains
steps.facts: a platform fact for each decision that affects the platform

changes.9: an intent is reviewed before the owner approves it, and the approval refuses one whose docs changed since the review (docs: Intake)
changes.8: a request naming two or more kinds of user gets a persona for each, and each persona a story citing the intent's requirements (docs: Elaboration checks)
changes.7: intents settle every surface of the corner checklist, follow up vague answers, and end with a read-back the owner confirms (docs: Elaboration checks)
changes.6: intents name the owner's requests, every goal line, story and requirement statement cites its source, and every request sentence is cited (docs: Intake)
changes.5: acceptance criteria read Given/When/Then, requirements are stated in EARS, and decisions follow MADR 4.0 (docs: Standard formats)
changes.4: bolts bind one domain outside increment 1, increment 1 holds the delivery module, fix bolts have one AC, and escape hatches may expire (docs: Construction by proof)
changes.3: intents declare a pathway and its steps (answered questions, domain docs, platform facts), a size, and decisions that cohere (docs: Inception)
changes.2: intents ship # Increments with ids I-<n>.<k>; work items are bolts B-<n> under bolts/; modules take a kind; the profile takes system (docs: Canonical model)

words.meaning: the shared platform every extension uses
a vertical capability owned elsewhere, built only against published contracts
a bounded context: its data, language, contract and events
one operation (command or query) of one domain, end to end, in one folder
a position inside a module: `interface`, `application`, `model` or `infrastructure`
one business outcome, with its why and success measures
a shippable step of an intent; increment 1 is the walking skeleton
the smallest build cycle: one card, worktree, review and merge
one regression, one AC that fails before the fix
quick, standard or full; decides which grid rows run
the generated brief one builder works from and one reviewer checks against
the main session running the loop
the human who approves, releases and rolls back

retired.sense: a piece of the architecture, not the docs bundle

retired.use: domain, or runtime for a deployable
